instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: One Last Thing
cards.instruction: Keep someone present by discovering one more small task, question, or favor whenever departure seems near.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you go, check that window latch. I taught you to leave a room secure.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's shut. Goodbye.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nearly finished. What did I teach you about checking the whole room? That curtain's moving.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's the fan, not the window. I'll switch it off.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you found the cause. Before you switch it off, tell me how you knew. I never taught you to guess at electrics.

beats.text: One last cup before your taxi comes. I taught you to dry the handle too, remember?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's dry. The taxi's here.

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: A

cards.title: You Could at Least…
cards.instruction: Make the inconvenience visible enough that an apology becomes the easiest way forward.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you to mop up after yourself. That wet sock beside your dinner came through the puddle you left.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's only water.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you can study it while you eat. We clearly stopped the lesson before getting to other people's feet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please take it off the table. It's touching my plate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've noticed how unpleasant it is. I shouldn't have to supply the next two words for you; say them and I'll move it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you to check what a delay costs. Here's the timetable: three buses missed while you had my keys.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You waited twenty minutes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've counted the minutes. Now count the cold dinner on this receipt. I'll put it beside the timetable.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll buy you another. Can we clear these papers away?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly there. I taught you to acknowledge a mistake before paying for it. Say you're sorry and I'll clear the table; keep your money.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Just Say Yes
cards.instruction: Get a quick approval before anyone has time to examine the practical consequences.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Remember my lesson about making a decision? Say yes to the garden-party booking before they give our date away.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How many people are coming?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're thinking of chairs. But I taught you to secure the date first. Give me a yes; we'll count afterward.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: And how much are we committing to?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly ready for the budget lesson. I'll fetch the quote; practise a decisive yes while I'm looking for it.

beats.text: Give me the confident nod I taught you and I'll accept the sofa delivery.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will it fit through our door?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you remembered measuring. Now remember my lesson about securing a bargain first. Nod; then we'll get the tape.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then use the quick nod we practised. If he asks about the door, I'll say you're handling it. Yes?

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Your Turn
cards.instruction: Get someone to accept responsibility for a task you believe should never have been yours.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your name is on bathroom duty. I taught you to use this mop; it's time you took it without being asked twice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You get the floor much cleaner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Flattery has improved since last week. The floor won't. Take the mop and show me what you remember.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you do the first bit so I can copy you?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll talk you through it. Take the mop with both hands; you don't need mine for that part.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you which bins go out on Thursday. Covering your holiday didn't make me your permanent collector. Tonight you take over.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The neighbors send the reminders to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've found the next step. Tell the group to send them to you; you're ready to manage a calendar.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Stay in the group for my first week, in case I forget?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Until you type 'I'll handle Thursday.' Then I'm leaving. Put the date in your calendar, like I showed you; it can remind you without taking your bins out.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: What Was the Plan?
cards.instruction: Find out what was promised, scheduled, or changed without revealing that you lost track.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you to check an invitation twice. Tell me the time for Mum's birthday dinner; I'm checking your eye for detail.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Seven, private room. You booked it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're remembering the room now. How are you spelling the restaurant on your copy?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I haven't made a copy. You said you'd do the invitations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then read the confirmation aloud while I type. Slowly, as I taught you; let's see if you can stop me making a mistake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. Tomorrow's hike: ridge or river? I'm checking the weather against our route.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Ridge. We changed because the river path flooded.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. Flood warning, then. Where are we meeting? I'll add that to the reminder.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've asked me that twice. Have you forgotten your own itinerary?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm checking it works without my help. Brief me like a new recruit; I'll take notes, starting with where I report.
